Drop matches on a floor, and counting them can find pi.
Each match is exactly as long as a floorboard is wide.
What share land across a crack?
Most of them: about two in three.
Here's why: bend a wire into a hoop as wide as a board.
Wherever it lands, it crosses the cracks twice.
Straighten it: it's pi matches long.
Cut it into matches and scatter them: still two crossings, on average.
So each match has a two-in-pi chance: sixty-four percent.
Count the crossings, and you can estimate pi.
Twenty thousand matches: three point one four.
